title: Chapter 87 — The Referral & Review Engine
intro: The referral ask, the review system, and advocate cultivation.

sections.title: When to Ask
sections.content:
The best time to ask for a referral is during the 48-hour post-delivery call when the customer is excited about their new appliance. 'Is everything working great? Fantastic. By the way, if you know anyone shopping for appliances, I would love the chance to help them.'

The second-best time is at the 30-day follow-up. The third is at one year. You have three natural windows — use all of them.

sections.title: The Review Ask
sections.content:
One bad Google review can cost you more than a hundred good sales days. Building a review culture is essential.

Make it easy. Send a direct link to your Google review page. Time it right — 48 hours to one week after delivery, when satisfaction is highest. Keep it simple: 'Would you mind leaving a quick review? It helps our store and it helps me personally.'

When responding to negative reviews, never get defensive. Acknowledge the issue, take it offline, and resolve it. Other potential customers are reading your response — they are evaluating how you handle problems, not whether you are perfect.

sections.title: Building Advocates
sections.content:
A happy customer is good. An advocate is a revenue machine. Advocates actively recommend you to friends, family, neighbours, and coworkers. They post photos of their new kitchen. They tag your store on social media.

You build advocates through exceptional post-sale service. The follow-up calls. The proactive water filter reminders. The personal touch on every interaction. When a customer feels like you genuinely care about their experience — not just the sale — they become your unpaid marketing team.
